newsitem.title: USA: Three Georgia cops wounded in armed standoff.
newsitem.headline: Three Georgia cops wounded in armed standoff.

text.p: Three Georgia police detectives were wounded Saturday in a 15-minute gun battle with a heavily armed man holed up in a rural mobile home northwest of Augusta, authorites said.

Shots rang out along state Highway 79 just after 10 a.m. EST, when agents from the Georgia Bureau of Investigation tried to end a standoff that had begun Friday, by lobbing tear gas cannisters into the residence.

The gunman, identified as Wayne Miller, fired on police with what appeared to be a shotgun and then tossed out a hand grenade. The grenade did not explode. But three GBI agents were injured in the melee. They were treated at a hospital in nearby Augusta and released.
"Gunfire ensued for 10 to 15 minutes. Prior to that, he threw out a hand grenade and that's when law enforcement returned fire," said GBI spokeswoman Pamela Swanson.

Local press reports later said the gunman's mother tried to help police talk him out. When Miller failed to respond to the entreaties, GBI agents prepared to send in a remote-controlled robot equipped with a camera to determine his condition and his whereabouts.
Miller was described by police as a man in his late 40s who lived alone at the mobile home.

The standoff began Friday after state police and Lincoln County sheriff's deputies arrested another man in an undercover drug bust that netted two to three pounds of marijuana. A search of that suspect's home revealed another 30 to 35 pounds of marijuana and evidence which police said could identify Miller as the source of the controlled substance.
Miller pulled a gun on GBI agents who went to his home to question him about the drug case and the standoff ensued.
Lincolnton is located about 100 miles east of Atlanta.
